facts.text: Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre is Thunder Bay's largest employer with over 2,800 employees and an annual budget of more than $300 million.

Thunder Bay is the service and supply hub for Northwestern Ontario's mining industry, with 10 active mines, over 18 major exploration projects and more than 400 local mine service and supply companies.
facts.publisher: Thunder Bay Community Economic Development Commission

facts.text: Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre is a 375-bed acute care facility, the Regional Trauma Centre and Cancer Referral Centre for Northwestern Ontario, and runs the second busiest emergency room in Canada.
facts.publisher: Thunder Bay Community Economic Development Commission

facts.text: Lakehead University's main campus in Thunder Bay has about 7,900 students and is home to the Bora Laskin Faculty of Law and the western campus of the Northern Ontario School of Medicine.
Major employers include Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre, Lakehead District School Board, Bombardier Transportation, Resolute Forest Products and Lakehead University.

overview: Thunder Bay counted 108,843 residents in the 2021 Census, up just 0.9% from 107,909 in 2016. The median age is 44.0 and the median household income in 2020 was $77,500, so the customer base is older, stable and not expanding on its own.

The city's 48,405 occupied dwellings are spread over 327.77 square kilometres, and the economy rests on the regional hospital, Lakehead University and a mining supply sector of more than 400 companies. Local businesses win by holding loyal customers and serving the wider Northwestern Ontario region.
